cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Heroic Code and Divine Righteousness: Mortality, Honor, and Covenant
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In Homer's Iliad, Achilles' wrath (mênis) confronts the inexorable tragedy of human mortality and cosmic indifference, where honor (timê) and glory (kleos) are purchased with blood. Contrast this heroic ethos with the covenantal theology of The Hebrew Bible (Tanakh), examining how each text conceptualizes the relationship between divine sovereignty, human obedience, and the moral meaning of suffering.
rubricCriteria: Textual analysis of Achilles' rejection of Agamemnon's gifts versus biblical covenantal stipulations
Rigorous contrast between Homeric theophany and biblical divine command
Examination of how human finitude and suffering are invested with meaning in both traditions

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Nostos, Polytropia, and the Moral Order of the Cosmos
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: While the Iliad examines battlefield mortality and existential fury, the Odyssey centers on homecoming (nostos), endurance, and cunning intelligence (mêtis/polytropia). Analyze how Odysseus' reclamation of Ithaca reconfigures justice and cosmic order in comparison to the covenantal restoration found in the prophetic narratives of The Hebrew Bible and the tragic fatalism of the Iliad.
rubricCriteria: Analysis of Odysseus' moral agency compared to Achilles' tragic intransigence
Evaluation of the restoration of domestic order alongside biblical prophetic visions of return
Examination of divine justice (dikê) in Homer versus covenantal justice (tsedeq) in the Tanakh

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: From Mythos to Logos: Rational Inquiry, Epistemic Skepticism, and the Soul
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Drawing upon the foundational philosophical problems presented in Perry, Bratman & Fischer's Introduction to Philosophy, evaluate how formal analytical inquiry (epistemology, personal identity, and the problem of evil) marks a methodological rupture from the mythopoetic explanations of Homer (Iliad, Odyssey) and the scriptural revelations of The Hebrew Bible.
rubricCriteria: Formulation of the transition from narrative/theological authority to dialectical reason
Critique of personal identity and moral accountability across Homeric and philosophical models
Analysis of the problem of unjustified suffering in systematic philosophy versus the Book of Job

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Normative Grounds of Obligation: Deontology, Teleology, and Moral Sentiment
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Using the selections in Shafer-Landau's Ethical Theory: An Anthology, construct a critical dialogue between modern normative frameworks (virtue ethics, consequentialism, contractualism) and the moral architectures encountered earlier in the curriculum. How do secular philosophical accounts of obligation challenge or formalize both Homeric shame culture and biblical divine command theory?
rubricCriteria: Comparative evaluation of divine command theory versus autonomous rational ethics
Contrast between Homeric honor-based virtue and modern virtue ethics / utilitarianism
Coherent argumentation regarding the grounding of moral obligations

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Historian's Craft: Evidence, Time, and the Reconstruction of the Past
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In The Historian's Craft, Marc Bloch argues that history is the "science of men in time," demanding critical cross-examination of involuntary evidence rather than passive chronicle. Analyze Bloch's historical methodology against the historiographical assumptions embedded in the biblical historical books (Tanakh) and Homeric epic memory, demonstrating how historical criticism establishes epistemic validity.
rubricCriteria: Contrast between Bloch's critical method and providential / epic historical narrative
Analysis of involuntary testimony and historical witnesses
Evaluation of the epistemic status of historical truth versus philosophical certainty

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Microhistory, Cosmology, and Popular Belief: The Menocchio Case
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In The Cheese and the Worms, Carlo Ginzburg investigates the inquisitorial trials of the miller Menocchio to unearth popular culture and peasant cosmogony. Compare Ginzburg's microhistorical method with Bloch's overarching structural craft (The Historian's Craft), evaluating how both authors challenge monolithic interpretations of religious authority originally articulated in scriptural and philosophical traditions.
rubricCriteria: Critique of elite versus popular appropriations of sacred texts
Methodological comparison between Ginzburg's microhistory and Bloch's comparative method
Analysis of inquisitorial documentation as historical evidence

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Power, Silence, and the Production of History
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Michel-Rolph Trouillot demonstrates in Silencing the Past that historical production is inherently entwined with power at four distinct moments: the making of sources, the making of archives, the making of narratives, and the making of history. Interrogate Trouillot's critique of historical silencing in light of Marc Bloch's craft, Homer's selective epic commemorations, and biblical canonical formation.
rubricCriteria: Application of Trouillot's four silences to early foundational texts and archives
Dialogue with Bloch and Ginzburg on archival bias and subaltern voices
Philosophical reflection on memory, erasure, and historical responsibility

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Finitude of Kingship: Mortality and Civilization in Gilgamesh
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: The Epic of Gilgamesh explores the agony of Enkidu's death and Gilgamesh's futile quest for bodily immortality. Synthesize this Mesopotamian meditation on civilization, friendship, and mortality with the Homeric tragic vision in the Iliad and the covenantal anthropology of Genesis in The Hebrew Bible, examining how early civilizations reconciled human grandeur with unavoidable extinction.
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.analyticalMode: Archaic Epic Comparison and Existential Anthropology
rubricCriteria: Comparative analysis of Gilgamesh's and Achilles' responses to the death of their companions
Contrast between the Mesopotamian underworld and Sheol/Hades
Examination of urban civilization versus wild nature in archaic thought

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Inquiry into the Human Condition: Herodotus, Epic Memory, and Cultural Pluralism
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Herodotus opens his Histories claiming to preserve the memory of great deeds while investigating the causes of conflict between Greeks and non-Greeks. Evaluate how Herodotus transforms Homeric epic storytelling and archaic chronicles into an empirical inquiry (historiê) of human customs, fortune (tychê), and hubris, synthesizing his approach with Bloch's historical craft.
rubricCriteria: Differentiation of Herodotean historiê from epic kleos and poetic myth
Analysis of custom (nomos) as "king of all" across Persian, Egyptian, and Greek perspectives
Evaluation of divine retribution (nemesis) and human causality

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Power, Realpolitik, and Human Nature in Thucydides
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Thucydides explicitly claims his History of the Peloponnesian War is a possession for all time (ktêma es aiei) because human nature remains constant. Contrast Thucydides' rigorous political realism, speech-act reconstructions, and clinical diagnosis of stasis (civil strife) with Herodotus' ethnographic inquiry and Homer's heroic worldview.
rubricCriteria: Detailed analysis of the Melian Dialogue and the Athenian justification of empire
Contrast between Thucydidean secular political causality and Herodotean divine envy
Critique of the collapse of democratic discourse during plague and revolution

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Fate, Hubris, and Civic Crisis in Greek Tragedy
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Drawing upon Greek Tragedies (Sophocles, Euripides), examine how Athenian drama interrogates the conflicting claims of kinship, civic law, and divine command. Contrast the tragic dilemmas of Antigone and Oedipus with the moral obligations of biblical covenant (Tanakh) and the heroic imperatives of the Homeric epic.
rubricCriteria: Contrast between divine/unwritten law in Antigone and biblical Torah
Analysis of tragic knowledge (pathei mathos) versus epic prowess
Evaluation of the political resonance of tragedy in democratic Athens after Thucydides

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: From Blood Vengeance to Civic Justice: Aeschylus' Oresteia
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Aeschylus' Oresteia traces the transition from the private vendetta of the Furies to the civic jurisprudence of the Areopagus under Athena's guidance. Synthesize this transformation with the legal codes of The Hebrew Bible and Thucydides' portrait of legal breakdown in Corcyra, analyzing whether civic justice successfully redeems archaic violence.
rubricCriteria: Transformation of archaic retribution into institutionalized civic trial
Comparison with biblical lex talionis and cities of refuge
Assessment of the gender dynamics and patriarchal resolution of the trial of Orestes

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Examined Life and the Athenian Polis: The Trial and Death of Socrates
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In Plato's Apology, Crito, and Phaedo, Socrates defines philosophy as care of the soul (epimeleia psyches) and preparation for death, refusing to compromise his divine calling before the Athenian jury. Reconstruct Socrates' defense against the background of the Peloponnesian War (Thucydides) and the traditional piety of Homeric and tragic literature.
rubricCriteria: Contrast between Socratic elenchus and Sophistic rhetoric in Thucydides
Socrates' conception of citizenship and obedience to law in Crito versus Antigone
The philosophical redefinition of virtue (aretê) against traditional aristocratic honor

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Architecture of the Just Soul and the Kallipolis: Plato's Republic
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In the Republic, Plato constructs the ideal city in speech (Kallipolis) through a rigorous analogy between the tripartite soul and the tripartite state, culminating in the rule of the philosopher-king and the Allegory of the Cave. Critique Plato's vision of justice against the political realities of Thucydides and the archaic covenantal society of The Hebrew Bible.
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.analyticalMode: Systematic Political Philosophy and Epistemic Metaphysics
rubricCriteria: Critique of Thrasymachus' definition of justice alongside the Melian Dialogue
Analysis of the Theory of Forms and the Cave as a departure from poetic mimesis
Comparative evaluation of Plato's philosopher-king with biblical prophetic leadership

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Teleology, Eudaimonia, and the Polis: Aristotle's Ethics and Politics
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Aristotle defines human flourishing (eudaimonia) as an activity of the soul in accordance with complete virtue, arguing in the Politics that the human being is by nature a political animal (zôon politikon). Contrast Aristotle's teleological ethics with Plato's transcendent Form of the Good (Republic) and the deontological and consequentialist theories studied in modern ethics (Shafer-Landau).
rubricCriteria: Contrast between Aristotelian immanent teleology and Platonic transcendent Forms
Analysis of the doctrine of the mean and phronêsis (practical wisdom)
Critical assessment of Aristotle's natural teleology regarding women, slaves, and citizenship

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Empire, Pietas, and the Burden of Destiny: Virgil's Aeneid
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Virgil's Aeneid appropriates Homeric epic to provide an ideological and mythological foundation for Augustan Rome, casting Aeneas as an emblem of dutiful devotion (pietas) subordinated to historical destiny. Synthesize Virgil's tragic celebration of imperium with Homer's individualistic Achilles (Iliad), Thucydides' critique of imperial hubris, and Plato's philosopher-state.
rubricCriteria: The transformation of Homeric heroic timê into Roman imperial pietas and labor
The cost of empire illustrated through the tragedies of Dido and Turnus
Virgil's historical teleology contrasted with Thucydidean cyclical realism

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Metamorphosis, Eros, and Cosmic Instability: Ovid versus the Epic Tradition
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In the Metamorphoses, Ovid presents a universe characterized by perpetual flux, tyrannical divine lust, and bodily transformation. Interrogate Ovid's subversive poetic cosmology as a direct challenge to Virgil's teleological Roman destiny (Aeneid), Homer's heroic cosmos (Iliad), and the theological creation narratives of Genesis (Tanakh).
rubricCriteria: Comparative analysis of cosmogony: Ovid's chaos/transformation versus Genesis and Hesiod
Ovid's portrait of capricious divine authority as veiled political critique of Augustan power
The instability of personal identity in Ovid contrasted with Homeric epic integrity

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Axiomatic Deduction and the Synthetic A Priori: Euclid's Elements
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Euclid's Elements establishes the paradigm of deductive mathematical demonstration, deriving complex geometrical truths from a minimal set of definitions, postulates, and common notions. Analyze the epistemic significance of the Euclidean method for philosophical certainty, comparing its rigorous demonstration with Platonic dialectic (Republic) and formal ethical reasoning (Shafer-Landau).
rubricCriteria: Analysis of Euclid's axiomatic method and the fifth postulate
Plato's use of geometry in Meno/Republic as a bridge to noesis and the Forms
The historical impact of Euclidean deduction on concepts of universal, necessary truth

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Dharma, Nishkama Karma, and Transcendent Duty in the Bhagavad Gita
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: In the Bhagavad Gita, Krishna instructs Arjuna on selfless action (nishkama karma), devotion (bhakti), and cosmic duty (svadharma) in the midst of fratricidal battlefield despair. Compare Arjuna's ethical crisis with Achilles' withdrawal in the Iliad and Socrates' adherence to moral duty in Plato's Crito, evaluating how different civilizations ground action in cosmic order.
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.analyticalMode: Comparative Duty Ethics and Metaphysics of Action
rubricCriteria: Contrast between nishkama karma and Western consequentialist / deontological frameworks
Arjuna's moral grief compared to Achilles' wrath and heroic pride
The theophany of Vishvarupa contrasted with the biblical theophany in Job / Exodus

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Ritual, Filial Piety, and Moral Cultivation: Confucius' Analects
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Confucius anchors human flourishing and social harmony in ritual propriety (li), humaneness (ren), and the self-cultivation of the exemplary person (junzi). Contrast the Ruist vision of virtuous governance through moral radiance with Plato's philosopher-ruler (Republic), Aristotle's virtue ethics (Ethics), and biblical covenantal law (Tanakh).
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.analyticalMode: Comparative Virtue Ethics and Social Philosophy
rubricCriteria: The role of ritual (li) as embodied ethical discipline versus Platonic abstract Forms
Governance by moral authority (de) versus rule by legal punishment (fa) or coercion
Filial piety (xiao) and familial embeddedness versus universal philosophical claims

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: Human Nature and the Sprouts of Goodness: Mencius
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Mencius defends the innate goodness of human nature (xing shan), using the parable of the child at the well to argue that moral sprouts (four seeds) require benevolent political and agricultural nurturing. Contrast Mencius' moral optimism with Thucydides' pessimistic assessment of human nature during war and the biblical narrative of the human heart after Eden.
rubricCriteria: Reconstruction of the Mencian debate on human nature and the four moral sprouts
Contrast with Thucydidean realpolitik and biblical doctrine of original sin/corruption
Mencius' doctrine of the Mandate of Heaven and the right to depose tyrannical rulers

cumulativeSynthesisEssay.title: The Dao, Spontaneity, and Skeptical Freedom in Classical Asian Philosophy
cumulativeSynthesisEssay.prompt: Synthesize the mystical and skeptical insights of Laozi's Daodejing and Zhuangzi's Inner Chapters with the Ruist humanism of Confucius and Mencius. How does Daoist non-action (wuwei) and perspective relativism challenge both Confucius' ritual order and the rationalist teleology of Greek philosophy (Plato, Aristotle)?
rubricCriteria: Detailed contrast between Confucian artificial cultivation and Daoist natural uncarved block (pu)
Zhuangzi's butterfly dream and skepticism compared with Socratic ignorance and Plato's Cave
Political critique of statecraft and war in the Daodejing
